topic.title: Federated Optimization under Heterogeneity and Communication Constraints
topic.overview: Federated optimization trains across clients whose data, availability, and computing resources differ. The represented methods reduce communication, correct local-update drift, adapt optimization, and account for partial participation. These are coupled problems because saving synchronization can amplify differences between clients.
topic.whyItMatters: Keeping data local does not make distributed optimization simple or automatically private. Practical performance requires methods that tolerate slow devices and uneven sampling while preserving the intended statistical objective.
topic.evolution: The 2017 multi-task perspective explicitly considers systems heterogeneity. Subsequent work develops drift correction and arbitrary communication patterns, followed by compressed adaptive methods and stronger participation guarantees. Recent approaches combine parameter-free updates, error feedback, and resource-adaptive fine-tuning. The evidence suggests several ways to reduce coordination costs, each tied to assumptions about sampling and heterogeneity.
openQuestions: How can guarantees remain useful when participation correlates with client data?
When do communication savings outweigh the bias introduced by longer local training?

papers.tldr: FedGMR gradually expands client sub-models to improve convergence and accuracy in heterogeneous federated learning.

papers.title: Class-Grouped Normalized Momentum and Faster Hyperparameter Exploration to Tackle Class Imbalance in Federated Learning
papers.tldr: FedCGNM balances class-group updates in federated learning, while FedHOO efficiently tunes resampling rates for smaller federations.

papers.title: DecFus: Decentralized Layer-wise Fusion with Dynamic Exploration and Exploitation
papers.tldr: DecFus dynamically combines layer exchange and averaging to improve decentralized training and proves convergence without a doubly stochastic aggregation requirement.

papers.title: Delayed Momentum Aggregation: Communication-efficient Byzantine-robust Federated Learning with Partial Participation
papers.tldr: DeMoA combines cached and fresh client momentum to maintain Byzantine robustness when only a subset of clients participates.

papers.title: DREAM: A Unified Framework for Drift-Corrected Federated Multi-Objective Learning
papers.tldr: DREAM jointly corrects client drift and task aggregation bias in federated learning with conflicting objectives.

papers.title: Federated Bilevel Performative Prediction
papers.tldr: The paper develops federated bilevel learning methods for decision-dependent data distributions, with conditional stability guarantees and supporting experiments.

papers.title: FedQueue: Queue-Aware Federated Learning for Cross-Facility HPC Training
papers.tldr: FedQueue incorporates HPC queue predictions and update staleness into federated training to improve convergence efficiency and elapsed training time.

papers.title: FedScar: Correcting Geometric Bias for Flatness-Consistent Federated Learning
papers.tldr: FedScar corrects persistent differences in client loss geometry to improve global flatness and generalization without extra communication.

papers.title: FedVeer: Self-Adaptive Skew Estimation for Robust Federated Learning
papers.tldr: FedVeer estimates client skew with adaptive neighborhoods and filtered margins to improve federated learning under uneven and noisy updates.

papers.title: HO-SFL: Hybrid-Order Split Federated Learning with Backprop-Free Clients and Dimension-Free Aggregation
papers.tldr: HO-SFL pairs server backpropagation with client zeroth-order updates to reduce memory and communication while retaining comparable convergence speed.

papers.title: LS$^2$MC-GDA: A Smoothed Algorithm for Federated Stochastic Multi-Level Compositional Minimax Optimization
papers.tldr: LS²MC-GDA combines smoothing and variance reduction to improve theoretical sample and communication complexity for federated compositional minimax optimization.

papers.title: Robust Federated Learning Against Adaptive Compression
papers.tldr: ParFreFL and ComParFreFL reduce federated-learning communication while preserving parameter-free operation and supporting heterogeneous, partially participating clients.

papers.title: Server-Proximal Aggregation for Federated Domain-Incremental Learning under Partial Participation: Task-Uniform Convergence and Backward Transfer
papers.tldr: SPECIAL anchors federated updates to the previous global model, bounding earlier-task deterioration and providing task-uniform convergence guarantees as domains change.

papers.title: UB-SMoE: Universally Balanced Sparse Mixture-of-Experts for Resource-adaptive Federated Fine-tuning of Foundation Models
papers.tldr: UB-SMoE balances expert use and restores learning signals to inactive experts, improving federated fine-tuning for resource-constrained clients.
